dialog.0: What happened to that soup from yesterday?
dialog.4: Fuck, that soup was mine. I was saving it for today.
dialog.6: Maria, it's soup. Buy another one.
dialog.10: You could really go to the grocery store and buy some more stuff.
dialog.11: Buy rice, potatoes, bread, coffee, cooking oil, chicken, eggs, sugar, and some fruit.
dialog.12: But why coffee? We still have some.
dialog.15: Then it must be hiding in the deepest depths of hell.
dialog.16: At least hell is a more pleasant place than my workplace.
dialog.17: While you're there, bring me some shampoo. I ran out today.
dialog.18: Could you come with me, then?
dialog.24: You have an exam the day after tomorrow.
dialog.26: I studied. I stayed up all night.
dialog.28: About the shampoo. Get that Reimondi one.
dialog.30: It's the only one that's any good.
dialog.31: Damn, you use the most expensive one.
dialog.32: Are you really going to start arguing about shampoo now?
dialog.33: Maria, this one costs four times as much.
dialog.36: By the way, where's my card?
dialog.37: On the table. Where you always leave it.
dialog.39: Do you want a soda? I'm really craving a soda.
dialog.40: I don't really want one, but if you want one, you can bring one.
dialog.41: I'm heading out. I'll be right back.
dialog.42: Make sure you don't forget my fucking shampoo again!
dialog.43: Oh my God, what have I done?
dialog.44: Damn. I'm going to have to put some things back. I don't have much money.
dialog.45: Of course, sir. Take your time.
dialog.46: I think I can take this out. I'll buy it another day.
dialog.51: Where did you get a gun?
dialog.52: I've always wanted to see Mom shoot, but I never got the chance.
dialog.53: She taught me a little. Every once in a while, I go out and practice in the forest.
dialog.54: How long have you been doing this?
dialog.56: And you've been hiding this from me all this time?
dialog.57: I wasn't hiding it from you. I just hadn't shown you yet.
dialog.58: Okay. I'm tired. Wanna play for a bit?
dialog.59: Okay. Let's play Mortal Kombat: Armageddon.
dialog.63: You're the one who doesn't know how to play.
dialog.64: You just keep repeating the same combo.
dialog.65: And you keep falling for it.
dialog.67: Are you going to use the same combo?
dialog.75: If I want to pay the rent, yeah.
dialog.76: You could stop working so much.
dialog.77: And what are we supposed to live on?
dialog.79: You have an exam the day after tomorrow.
dialog.81: You know you don't have to.
dialog.82: I kind of already feel useless just studying all the time.
dialog.83: I wake up, study, study some more, sleep... and then I do it all over again the next day.
dialog.84: You're studying so you can have a better life. I've already studied everything I needed to get a "decent" job. You know that's what Dad wanted for both of us too.
dialog.87: It just doesn't feel like I'm living. I feel like dead weight.
dialog.88: I'll find a way to do something. At least so we can have a little bit of dignity.
dialog.89: Okay, just promise me you won't drop out of college.
dialog.90: You know I'm terrible at keeping promises. But okay, I promise.
dialog.93: Long time no see, Mom. How are you doing?
dialog.97: Just spit it out. What do you want?
dialog.98: Look, Mom, both of us here are in a tough spot.
dialog.100: I haven't even told you what it is yet, you haven't even thought about it.
dialog.101: I thought about it before you even called.
dialog.102: Please Mom, listen to me, we need help.
dialog.104: You don't even know what I was going to ask for.
dialog.105: I know you're going to ask for money.
dialog.106: Maria, I'm paying for your college. What else do you want me to do?
dialog.107: Maybe act like my mother once in a while.
dialog.113: I barely have time to eat, let alone time for you.
dialog.116: For those who want to enter SURGEMD, just call [generic number].
dialog.117: SURGEMD will be solo in normal mode.
dialog.120: Surgemd will be played in teams of two on the Tundra map.
dialog.122: Mark, do you want to go to Surgemd? It's going to be a duo.
dialog.124: No, I genuinely think we should go.
dialog.127: You're already practically a zombie. How about we at least have a few good days, even if they're our last?
dialog.128: Besides, if we win, we can finally put an end to this monotony.
dialog.129: Maria. I'm afraid of getting shot.
dialog.130: Don't worry, I'll make sure we win.
dialog.131: Maria, the chances of winning are really low. It's one in fifty.
dialog.133: Besides, my paycheck comes tomorrow. I can't wait for my boss to call me.
dialog.136: Mark. I'm calling to let you know that I'm going to reduce your salary.
dialog.138: You don't do your fucking job properly.
dialog.139: But what did I do wrong for you to do that?
dialog.140: Doesn't matter. I'm reducing your salary.
dialog.141: So? Do you want to go to Surgemd?
dialog.142: After that, I'm willing to do anything to get out of this life.
dialog.143: I just don't want to die.
dialog.146: You work six days a week. I study all day. We barely ever leave the house.
dialog.147: And your solution is to enter a game where fifty people try to kill each other?
dialog.148: My solution is to do something different.
dialog.151: A bet where we could die.
dialog.152: Don't worry, we're not going to die.
dialog.154: Damn, Maria. That was fifty cents. You could've bought some candy with that at the corner store.
dialog.155: Besides, where the hell did you get a fucking revolver?
dialog.156: I bought it at the gun store nearby.
dialog.157: Judging by your training, I'd say it paid off.
dialog.158: How many shots at the wall did you land before hitting the coin?
dialog.160: How did you not miss a single shot?
dialog.164: I feel like I was born knowing how to do this.
dialog.165: Incredible. Another useful thing Mom passed down to you. / Ironically.
dialog.166: I think you just had the greatest idea of all time.
dialog.167: It's incredible how much you actually know what you're doing.
dialog.168: We're standing in the middle of the street at night, waiting for a bus to pick us up and take us to a place that's probably going to kill us.
dialog.170: There it is. Once we get on, there's no going back.
